21	func main() {
22		// Resolve version/commit from build info before anything reads them.
23		versioninfo.Load()
24	
25		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
26		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
27	
28		// Handle interrupt signals
29		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
30		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
31		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
32			signals = append(signals, syscall.SIGTERM)
33		}
34		signal.Notify(sigChan, signals...)
35		go func() {
36			// First signal: cancel the context so in-flight work unwinds
37			// cleanly. signal.Notify has disabled Go's default "signal
38			// terminates" behavior, so without the second read below a user
39			// who Ctrl-C's again during a slow/stuck shutdown (e.g. a keyring
40			// read blocked in a subprocess we can't cancel) would find every
41			// further Ctrl-C swallowed. The second read restores an escape
42			// hatch: signal again to force-exit.
43			//
44			// We remember which signal fired so the eventual termination
45			// re-raises that same signal — a SIGTERM (from a supervisor /
46			// container stop) must exit 143, not masquerade as a SIGINT 130.
47			sig := <-sigChan
48			procsignal.Store(sig)
49			if sig == os.Interrupt {
50				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nInterrupting… press Ctrl-C again to force quit.")
51			} else {
52				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nReceived termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.")
53			}
54			cancel()
55			<-sigChan
56			dieFromSignal(sig)
57		}()
58	
59		// Create and execute root command
60		rootCmd := cli.NewRootCmd()
61	
62		// Make managed-installed plugins discoverable by the kubectl-style
63		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
64		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
65		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
66		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
67		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
68		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
69		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
70		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)
71	
72		if handled, code := cli.MaybeRunPlugin(ctx, rootCmd, os.Args[1:]); handled {
73			cancel()
74			os.Exit(code)
75		}
76		restorePATH()
77	
78		// Retired env vars fail every built-in command up front; a removed knob
79		// must never be silently ignored. Plugins (above) are exempt — what they
80		// read is their business.
81		if err := api.RejectRemovedAuthEnv(); err != nil {
82			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
83			cancel()
84			os.Exit(1)
85		}

88		if err != nil {
89			var silent *cli.SilentError
90	
91			switch {
92			case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && procsignal.Load() != nil:
93				// A signal cancelled the root context (our handler fired) or a
94				// keyring read was aborted by Ctrl-C. Don't dump the raw
95				// transport/keyring cancellation string ("...: context canceled",
96				// "read access token: signal: interrupt") as if it were a failure
97				// — die quietly by re-raising the signal that triggered it (see
98				// dieFromSignal) so an enclosing `while ...; do entire; done` loop
99				// actually breaks on a single Ctrl-C, and a SIGTERM shutdown still
100				// exits 143.
101				//
102				// We gate on a signal having been recorded rather than on the
103				// error type alone: a context.Canceled that arose without a signal
104				// (e.g. an internally-cancelled sub-context) is a genuine error
105				// and must fall through to normal reporting, not masquerade as a
106				// user abort (which would also wrongly break an enclosing loop).
107				// procsignal is the shared source of truth written both by the
108				// handler above and by the keyring interrupt path; the latter
109				// records the signal on this same goroutine before returning, so
110				// this Load never races that write.
111				cancel()
112				dieFromSignal(terminatingSignal())
113			case errors.As(err, &silent):

115			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown command") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown flag"):

119				// cobra.ExactArgs) and surface as "accepts N arg(s), received M".
120				// Show the failing subcommand's usage so the user sees what it
121				// actually expects — rootCmd's usage isn't useful for a
122				// subcommand-level arg mismatch. ExecuteContextC returns the
123				// deepest matched command, which is the one that failed.
124				showSuggestion(executed, err)

126				// A server can reject any authenticated flow (login, token
127				// refresh, RFC 8693 exchange) because this build is too old.
128				// The handler replaces the raw cli_upgrade_required error with
129				// actionable guidance — an interactive update offer, or the
130				// update + rerun commands. Handled here so every command gets
131				// it without wrapping its own errors.
132				if !cli.OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired(ctx, rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err, os.Args) {
133					fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err)
134				}
135			}
136	
137			cancel()
138			os.Exit(1)
139		}
140		if cli.ShouldCheckCheckpointPolicyWarning(executed) {
141			cli.WarnCheckpointPolicyIfNeeded(ctx, rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(), versioninfo.Version)
142		}
143		cancel() // Cleanup on successful exit
144	}

146	// terminatingSignal returns the signal that cancelled the root context,
147	// defaulting to SIGINT when the cancellation came from something other than a
148	// recorded terminating signal (so a stray context.Canceled still exits 130).
149	// The recorded signal lives in the shared procsignal package, written by the
150	// handler goroutine (SIGINT/SIGTERM) and by the keyring interrupt path (SIGINT).
151	func terminatingSignal() os.Signal {
152		if s := procsignal.Load(); s != nil {
153			return s
154		}
155		return os.Interrupt
156	}
157	
158	// dieFromSignal terminates the process as if it had been killed by sig, rather
159	// than exiting normally. The distinction matters to an interactive shell: it
160	// only aborts a `while true; do entire ...; done` loop when the child is
161	// *killed by* SIGINT (WIFSIGNALED). A plain os.Exit(130) is an ordinary exit,
162	// so the loop keeps respawning entire and Ctrl-C never escapes it. Re-raising
163	// the actual signal also keeps a SIGTERM shutdown reporting the conventional
164	// 143 (not 130). We reset sig to its default disposition, re-raise it to
165	// ourselves, and briefly wait for delivery; if the re-raise can't be delivered
166	// (e.g. Windows, where signal-to-self is unsupported) we fall back to a
167	// conventional 128+signal exit so we never hang.
168	func dieFromSignal(sig os.Signal) {
169		signal.Reset(sig)
170		if p, err := os.FindProcess(os.Getpid()); err == nil {
171			if err := p.Signal(sig); err == nil {
172				time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) // signal delivery ends the process well before this elapses
173			}
174		}
175		os.Exit(exitCodeForSignal(sig))
176	}
177	
178	// exitCodeForSignal maps a signal to the conventional 128+signum exit code
179	// (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM), falling back to 130 for a signal that
180	// doesn't carry a numeric value on this platform.
181	func exitCodeForSignal(sig os.Signal) int {
182		if s, ok := sig.(syscall.Signal); ok {
183			return 128 + int(s)
184		}
185		return 130
186	}
187	
188	// isPositionalArgError reports whether err looks like a cobra positional-
189	// arg validator failure. cobra's stock validators (ExactArgs, NoArgs,
190	// MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, RangeArgs) all surface error strings
191	// containing "arg(s)", and that substring doesn't appear in cobra's other
192	// error paths or in the cli's own errors — so it's a stable, cheap
193	// discriminator without reaching into cobra internals.
194	func isPositionalArgError(err error) bool {
195		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "arg(s)")
196	}

199		// Print usage first (brew style)
200		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())
201		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStderr(), "\nError: Invalid usage: %v\n", err)

# PR 1794 Review — `cli_upgrade_required` update hint

Verified locally: branch matches PR head, builds clean, all new tests pass.

## Overview

Server rejects old CLI with OAuth code `cli_upgrade_required` from any auth flow (login, refresh grant, RFC 8693). Before: raw error, no path forward. Now: central handler at `main.go` error arm replaces raw error with update offer (interactive) or copyable update+rerun commands (non-interactive). Refactor extracts shared update tail into `versioncheck/updateflow.go` (`PromptAllowed` gate + `RunUpdate`), reused by existing version-check nag. Re-exec after update marked with `ENTIRE_UPGRADE_RERUN=1` — loop guard prevents infinite update→rerun cycles, and stale-binary message names actual problem when installer wrote different file than running binary.

## Correctness — solid

- **Loop guard ordering right**: `IsPostUpdateRerun` checked before `canPrompt` in `offerCLIUpgrade`, so rerun child never re-prompts and gets stale-binary explanation instead of "update it" again.
- **Exit codes right**: successful re-exec exits with child code (`os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())` / `os.Exit(0)`); every failure leaf falls back to `main.go`'s `os.Exit(1)`. Installer failure skips rerun. Matches PR claims.
- **`errors.AsType[*exec.ExitError]`**: Go 1.26 API, go.mod says 1.26.4, compiles. Fine.
- **`MaybeAutoUpdate` gate swap safe**: `canAutoInstall()` inside `PromptAllowed` is redundant there (checked earlier at versioncheck.go:65) but harmless. Added `!IsPostUpdateRerun()` is intentional — suppresses version-check re-prompt right after update. Correct.
- **Switch arm ordering**: `SilentError` arm precedes default, so curated-message paths bypass handler — documented, acceptable gap.
- **Windows+unknown installer**: `UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary` returns downloads URL, `canAutoInstall` blocks prompt — consistent, no dead branch.

## Minor issues (non-blocking)

1. **Child killed by signal → exit 255, not 128+sig.** `updateflow.go:100` — child killed by SIGINT gives `ExitCode() = -1`, parent does `os.Exit(-1)` → 255. Shell loop won't break on Ctrl-C (main.go's `dieFromSignal` exists precisely for this). Also parent ctx cancel SIGKILLs child mid-cleanup (default `exec.CommandContext` Cancel). Edge case, low frequency — but a `WaitDelay`/`Cancel` override or signal-aware exit mapping would round it out.
2. **Substring match `IsCLIUpgradeRequired`.** Any error whose text contains `cli_upgrade_required` triggers takeover — e.g. server 500 body echoing the string. Comment explains why (auth-go has no sentinel); acceptable, but consider matching more anchored pattern (`oauth error: cli_upgrade_required`) if auth-go message shape is stable.
3. **`RerunCommandLine` quoting is Go-style, not shell.** Args with `$`, `*`, backticks pass unquoted — pasting back may re-expand. Display-only, tiny edge; fine to leave.
4. **`os.Exit` buried inside `RunUpdate`/`realReexecCommand`.** Skips `main.go`'s `cancel()`. Documented in doc comments ("does not return"), no deferred cleanup depends on it today — fine, just fragile if main ever grows deferred flush logic.

## Conventions & tests — good

- Accessibility: `NewAccessibleForm` used per CLAUDE.md convention. Non-interactive path prints complete copyable commands — agent-safe fallback rule satisfied.
- Seam-injection test pattern matches existing `autoupdate_test.go` style; `t.Parallel()` correctly omitted where package globals/env mutated, present elsewhere.
- Coverage thorough: detection, passthrough, non-interactive block, yes/no/decline, installer failure, re-exec failure, loop guard, argv reconstruction. Missing only trivial cases: stale-binary with empty argv (`"this binary"` fallback), and thin `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` wiring — both fine to skip.
- No duplication: single `RunUpdate` implementation confirmed; refactor genuinely unifies the two triggers.

## Security

- Re-exec re-resolves `argv[0]` via `LookPath` — runs whatever PATH now points at, same trust model as installer itself. Env marker only additive. `sh -c` installer execution pre-existing. No new concerns.

## Verdict

Ship it. Design careful, loop guard well thought out, tests match implementation. Minor items above optional follow-ups — signal exit-code mapping (#1) most worth doing eventually.
fix 1 and 4

Fix 1 (signal exit-code mapping + graceful cancel) and fix 4 (no `os.Exit` inside library — propagate exit code to main.go). Plan: `reexec` seam returns `(int, error)`, `RunUpdate` returns `(exitCode, exit bool)`, `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` returns `(handled, exitCode)`, main.go owns the single `os.Exit`.

## Fix 1 — signal-aware exit codes + graceful cancel (`updateflow.go`)

- Signal-killed rerun child now maps to shell convention `128+signum` (SIGINT → 130) via `WaitStatus.Signaled()`, instead of `os.Exit(-1)` → 255. Weird `-1`-but-not-signaled falls back to 1.
- Ctrl-C no longer SIGKILLs child mid-cleanup: `cmd.Cancel` forwards `os.Interrupt`, `WaitDelay = 5s` hard-kills a child that ignores it. On Windows the Signal call fails and WaitDelay kill applies — same one code path.

## Fix 4 — no `os.Exit` buried in library

Exit moved to main.go's single exit point; deferred/cleanup in callers now always runs:

- `realReexecCommand` returns `(int, error)` — child exit code, or error when spawn failed.
- `RunUpdate` returns `(exitCode int, rerun bool)` — `rerun=true` means original command was re-executed and caller should exit with `exitCode`; `false` (nil argv, installer failure, spawn failure) means caller keeps its own path. Version-check caller (`MaybeAutoUpdate`) ignores returns — nil argv never reruns.
- `OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired` returns `(handled bool, exitCode int)` — rerun child's code when update+retry ran, 1 on every other leaf.
- main.go: `exitCode := 1` before the switch, default arm overwrites when handled, single `cancel(); os.Exit(exitCode)`. Behavior unchanged on all failure leaves; successful update+retry still propagates child's code (including 0), now through main instead of deep inside `RunUpdate`.

## Tests

- Fixture `reexec` seam updated to `(int, error)`; added `reexecCode` field.
- New assertions: exit-code propagation through `RunUpdate` (child code 3) and through `offerCLIUpgrade` (exitCode 3 on accepted update, 1 on guidance leaves).
- New `TestRealReexecCommand_ExitCodes` (skipped on Windows): success → 0, `exit 3` → 3, SIGINT-killed → 130, unresolvable binary → error, nil argv → error. Exercises real spawn path including the new signal mapping.

## Why

`entire repo mirror list` only showed existing mirrors; the repos you *could* mirror were hidden behind a separate `--show-available` mode, with its own endpoint and its own table shape. `GET /repos?scope=all` returns existing mirrors and onboardable GitHub candidates in one discriminated shape — so the list can just show both.

## What

`entire repo mirror list` now also includes the repos that `--show-available` used to show. One table, rendered from a single `/repos?scope=all` call:

- **Mirrors** — clone URL + per-placement clone STATUS (`ready`/`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`); one row per mirror placement, so a multi-cell repo lists once per cell.
- **Candidates (repos that can be mirrored)** — ACCESS + an `available`/`owner-only` STATUS; no clone URL.
- Sparse cells render as `-`.
- The separate `--show-available` mode is gone: its rows are always included, and the flag itself is **removed** (errors as an unknown flag).
- `--json` emits the flat directory rows; the raw wire model stays at `entire api --to core /repos`.
- Truncated results warn on stderr (the endpoint has no pagination cursor).
- **Native (non-mirror) placements are dropped** — a repo created by `entire repo create` has no GitHub mirror clone URL, so it isn't listed in the mirror directory.

Every displayed column is sortable and filterable (client-side, before render):

| Column | `--sort` key | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| NAME (owner/repo) | `name` | `--name` (substring), `--owner` |
| CLONE URL | `clone-url` | `--cluster` (slug **or** public host) |
| PRIVATE | `private` | `--private` (tri-state) |
| STATUS | `status` | `--status` (exact) |
| ACCESS | `access` | `--access` (exact; candidates only) |

`--sort` takes a `-` prefix for descending; default is name ascending with a deterministic name+clone-URL tiebreak.

Placements carry only a cluster slug, so clone URLs are reconstructed by joining the slug against the cluster catalog (`ListClusters`).

## Depends on

Stacks on the coreapi schema regen + caller adaptations + cell fan-out fix, split out to **#1694** (merged to `main`).

## Test plan

- `go build ./...`, golangci-lint v2 (0 issues), full `cmd/entire/cli` package green.
- Covers: merged-list routing, all filters + sort (tiebreaks, case-insensitivity, tri-state `--private`), `buildRepoDir` (native-drop, multi-placement), `sortRepoDir`, `clusterHostBySlug`, truncated warning.

https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/815

## Why

`entire repo mirror list` only showed existing mirrors; the repos you *could* mirror were hidden behind a separate `--show-available` mode, with its own endpoint and its own table shape. `GET /repos?scope=all` returns existing mirrors and onboardable GitHub candidates in one discriminated shape — so the list can just show both.

## What

`entire repo mirror list` now also includes the repos that `--show-available` used to show. One table, one row per repo, rendered from a single `/repos?scope=all` call:

```
NAME (owner/repo)   CLUSTERS                              PRIVATE  STATUS   ACCESS
entirehq/entiredb   aws-us-east-2, aws-eu-central-1, +2   yes      ready    -
acme/marketing      -                                     no       available admin
```

- **Mirrors** — one row per repo (not per placement, so a four-cluster repo no longer occupies four rows). CLUSTERS lists the placement slugs; STATUS is the placements' shared clone status (`ready`/`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`) or `mixed` when they disagree.
- **Candidates (repos that can be mirrored)** — ACCESS + an `available`/`owner-only` STATUS; no clusters.
- Sparse cells render as `-`.
- The separate `--show-available` mode is gone: its rows are always included, and the flag itself is **removed** (errors as an unknown flag).
- `--json` emits the directory rows with nested `placements: [{cluster, status, cloneUrl}]`; the raw wire model stays at `entire api --to core /repos`.
- Truncated results warn on stderr (the endpoint has no pagination cursor).
- **Native (non-mirror) placements are dropped** — a repo created by `entire repo create` has no GitHub mirror clone URL, so it isn't listed in the mirror directory.
- A placement on a cluster the catalog can't resolve names its slug in CLUSTERS (no clone URL is fabricated for it).

**Per-cluster drill-down**: `entire repo mirror get` now also accepts the NAME cell verbatim — `<owner>/<repo>` — and lists that repo's mirror on every cluster with per-cluster clone URL and status (ULID and clone-URL forms unchanged). The list footer hints this on stderr (skipped for `--json` and empty tables):

```
Per-cluster detail and clone URLs: entire repo mirror get <owner/repo>
```

Every displayed column is sortable and filterable (client-side, before render):

| Column | `--sort` key | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| NAME (owner/repo) | `name` | `--name` (substring), `--owner` |
| CLUSTERS | `clusters` | `--cluster` (slug **or** public host, matching any placement) |
| PRIVATE | `private` | `--private` (tri-state) |
| STATUS | `status` | `--status` (exact; matches any placement, so `--status failed` surfaces a repo whose cell reads `mixed`) |
| ACCESS | `access` | `--access` (exact; candidates only) |

`--sort` takes a `-` prefix for descending; default is name ascending with a deterministic name+clusters tiebreak.

Placements carry only a cluster slug, so clone URLs are reconstructed by joining the slug against the cluster catalog (`ListClusters`).

## Depends on

Stacks on the coreapi schema regen + caller adaptations + cell fan-out fix, split out to **#1694** (merged to `main`).

- `go build ./...`, golangci-lint v2 (0 issues), full `cmd/entire/cli` package green, `mise run test:ci` green.
- Covers: merged-list routing, grouping (multi-placement single row, mixed-status roll-up, native-drop, unresolvable-slug), all filters + sort (any-placement `--cluster`/`--status`, tiebreaks, case-insensitivity, tri-state `--private`), `mirror get <owner/repo>` (server-side owner narrowing, client-side repo match, not-found error), detail-hint gating, truncated warning.
